evidence_classes.OFFICIAL_CONTROL_SURFACE: Law/regulator statement describing Russian control scope.
evidence_classes.ADJACENT_RUSSIAN_DPI_SORM_EXPORT: Verified foreign deployment/export of Russian interception/filtering technology that is not automatically TSPU.
evidence_classes.ROUTING_COLLATERAL_MODEL: Academic evidence for foreign traffic being affected when paths traverse censoring jurisdictions.
evidence_classes.US_ROUTING_DEFENSE_CONTROL: US defensive routing-security guidance relevant to preventing external redirection.
evidence_classes.NEGATIVE_CONTROL: Evidence constraining or weakening the external-TSPU hypothesis.

records.finding: FOCI 2026 documents broad Russian TSPU QUIC censorship and transition to SNI-dependent QUIC filtering, showing that TSPU is adaptable and protocol-aware.
records.claim_ceiling: Demonstrates TSPU behavior on Russian network paths; does not establish foreign TSPU deployment.

records.finding: Recorded Future identified at least eight Russian SORM providers exporting to Central Asia and Latin America and at least fifteen telecommunications companies as likely customers; major providers also market across Africa and the Middle East.
records.claim_ceiling: Confirms Russian surveillance-technology diffusion; SORM export is not proof of Roskomnadzor TSPU export or command-and-control.

records.finding: Recorded Future assesses that exported SORM systems can create data-security risk and notes concern that Russian manufacturers may retain access to systems deployed abroad; the degree of Russian access remains unclear.
records.claim_ceiling: Risk assessment, not proof that any specific foreign system is remotely operated by Russian authorities.

records.finding: Academic work shows ECMP and route changes can materially alter observed DNS/HTTP/HTTPS censorship, so any external-TSPU attribution must be path-stable and route-resolved.
records.claim_ceiling: General measurement methodology, not Russia-specific attribution.

records.finding: Research on Internet routing centralization shows foreign customer traffic may experience collateral censorship when routed through ASes under censoring jurisdictions, including Russia.
records.claim_ceiling: Establishes a plausible mechanism; does not prove a 2026 TSPU event.

records.finding: The FCC identifies BGP origin/path manipulation as a threat capable of redirecting, intercepting or blackholing US traffic and promotes RPKI/ROA/ROV and routing-risk management.
records.claim_ceiling: US defensive control; not evidence that TSPU currently manipulates BGP.

records.finding: CISA recommends strict prefix/AS-path filtering, maximum-prefix limits, routing authentication, route-change monitoring and protection of peering/control planes to reduce covert redirection risk.
records.claim_ceiling: Mitigation guidance applicable to route-manipulation scenarios; not TSPU attribution.

records.finding: The 2026 FOCI TSPU measurements constrain the demonstrated behavior to Russian-side network paths and do not show arbitrary censorship of foreign-origin users outside Russia.

The original WATCHERS investigation found no shared technical fingerprint linking the GitHub/OpenAI incidents to TSPU; GitHub published an internal Actions control-plane/database/event-processing cause for its main incident.
